qs.q:
Modern technology — Which person says…

A=Arthur (everything is a click away; social media good for communication; biggest priority = cyber-security; needs rules for vulnerable)
B=Betty (computer science student, geek; Gran on Facebook; big tech companies not paying taxes; must change with times)
C=Carlota (digital business makes her uneasy; social media = anxiety/depression in teens; too fast to keep up; work from home)
D=Damien (30-40 years ago = amazing change; information is power, now accessible; streaming artists get nothing = theft)
E=Ezra (generational divide: he uses Instagram/TikTok; grandparents watch TV; user content = too many untalented users)
F=Freya (both good and bad; can work from home; social media destroyed lives; robots took jobs; technology raised inequality)

0. everything is easy to get? [A=Arthur]
1. information technology has made the world more democratic?
2. social media is generally good for us?
3. social media causes mental health problems?
4. the biggest concern is cyber-security?
5. digital technology causes unemployment?
6. technology has raised the level of inequality?
7. the big tech companies have become too powerful?
8. Facebook is for middle-aged people?
9. their grandparents are addicted to social media?
10. digital technology has resulted in lower quality entertainment?
11. music streaming is equivalent to theft?
12. things are changing too quickly?
items: 1 — information technology has made the world more democratic?
2 — social media is generally good for us?
3 — social media causes mental health problems?
6 — technology has raised the level of inequality?
7 — the big tech companies have become too powerful?
9 — their grandparents are addicted to social media?
10 — digital technology has resulted in lower quality entertainment?
11 — music streaming is equivalent to theft?

qs.q:
A sudden genius

"Shouting for someone to hurl a football over the water, so he could MAKE A LEAPING CATCH."

Why did Derek ask his friends to throw the ball into the swimming pool?
A He wanted to play catch in the shallow end.
B He was trying to be in the centre of attention.
C The ladies forced him to do something risky for fun.
D He intended to jump after it and catch it while in the air.
opts: He wanted to play catch in the shallow end.
He was trying to be in the centre of attention.
The ladies forced him to do something risky for fun.
He intended to jump after it and catch it while in the air.

qs.q:
A sudden genius

"Doctors kept him there overnight FOR OBSERVATION."

Why was Derek kept in the hospital for the night?
A He needed a lot of sleep.
B He had lost a lot of blood.
C His mother insisted that he stay.
D He needed further medical supervision.
opts: He needed a lot of sleep.
He had lost a lot of blood.
His mother insisted that he stay.

qs.q:
A sudden genius

"As he approached the Casio, it was as if his body was INTUITIVELY READING THEM AS NOTES. His fingers flew across the keys, releasing an UNSTRUCTURED AND NEW, yet melodic, piece."

What is true of the music Derek started playing at Rick's house?
A It was a classical piece written by a known composer.
B It had a regular, recurring pattern of metre and melody.
C It was the product of images he'd seen in his mind's eye.
D It was from a music score he had found on the keyboard.
opts: It was a classical piece written by a known composer.
It had a regular, recurring pattern of metre and melody.
It was the product of images he'd seen in his mind's eye.
It was from a music score he had found on the keyboard.

qs.q:
A sudden genius

"His mind was CONTINUOUSLY AND UNBEARABLY FLOODED WITH SQUARES AND TUNES AND RHYTHMS. His hands were tapping out beats even in his sleep."

What was the most challenging problem for Derek after the accident?
A The music appeared without stopping.
B He suffered too many headaches.
C He had to live in the dark.
D He was partially deaf.
opts: He had to live in the dark.

qs.q:
A sudden genius

"His CURIOSITY WAS DISTURBED by the persistent fear that the ROOT OF IT ALL was something DEADLY that would bring his life to a halt."

What was Derek's biggest concern?
A That he would live his life in pain.
B That his condition has no explanation.
C That he would lose his sudden genius.
D That his gift was caused by a terminal illness.
opts: That he would live his life in pain.
That his condition has no explanation.
That he would lose his sudden genius.
That his gift was caused by a terminal illness.

qs.q:
A sudden genius

"When the left hemisphere is damaged, UNDAMAGED TISSUE IS RECRUITED FROM THE RIGHT HEMISPHERE as a way to COMPENSATE FOR THE LOSS."

How can the phenomenon Derek experienced be explained?
A It is a hidden potential in the left hemisphere of the brain.
B It is the consequence of the brain's ability to recover from trauma.
C It is an error in the connection between the two brain hemispheres.
D It is a consequence of too much online research about the condition.
opts: It is a hidden potential in the left hemisphere of the brain.
It is the consequence of the brain's ability to recover from trauma.
It is an error in the connection between the two brain hemispheres.
It is a consequence of too much online research about the condition.

H — But there are hopes machine learning could help in the future.
